slot.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slot.brief: EM wave of given intensity striking a surface (perfectly reflecting or absorbing); find radiation pressure/force via I/c or 2I/c.

stem: A plane electromagnetic wave of intensity 300 W m^-2 falls normally on a perfectly reflecting surface of area 2.0 m^2. The force exerted on the surface is (take c = 3 x 10^8 m s^-1)

verdicts.working: For a perfectly reflecting surface, radiation pressure is \(2I/c\). Thus \(F=(2I/c)A=2(300)(2.0)/(3\times10^8)=4.0\times10^{-6}\,\text{N}\).

working:
For a perfect reflector, radiation pressure p = 2I/c. Force F = pA = 2IA/c = 2 * 300 * 2.0 / (3 x 10^8) = 1200 / (3 x 10^8) = 4.0 x 10^-6 N.

Independent check: For a perfectly reflecting surface, radiation pressure is \(2I/c\). Thus \(F=(2I/c)A=2(300)(2.0)/(3\times10^8)=4.0\times10^{-6}\,\text{N}\).
solution:
For a perfectly reflecting surface, radiation pressure is $p=\dfrac{2I}{c}$. Hence,
$$F=pA=\dfrac{2IA}{c}=\dfrac{2(300)(2.0)}{3\times10^8}=4.0\times10^{-6}\,\text{N}.$$
